clue.text: Bird to hide nut, we hear, as a last course

parts.note: a goose is a common bird

indicators.note: says the word is to be taken by its sound, as heard rather than as written

parts.note: to hide something is to bury it
a nut is slang for a crazy person, a fool

explanation.surface: Someone gives a bird a nut to hide as they finish a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns BURY into its sound-alike BERRY. FOOL here means a nutcase, not the pudding word yet.
explanation.definitionFit: This creamy fruit purée dessert is served as the final course of a meal.

clue.text: The pillars of Northern Ireland

parts.note: reads like the leading citizens of the province, but means the basalt columns on the Antrim coast

explanation.surface: A tribute to the leading figures who hold up Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: Pillars sounds like worthy people; the clue really means the famous hexagonal basalt columns on the County Antrim coast.
explanation.definitionFit: This landmark is a mass of interlocking basalt columns standing on the coast of County Antrim.

clue.text: Waterproof worn round one links when stormy

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: stormy suggests a turbulent tossing, so these letters are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: A golfer pulls on rain gear before a round on the links in bad weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when stormy' scrambles O, I and LINKS together. 'worn' is a link here, though it suits a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: An oilskin is a coat made waterproof with oil, worn by sailors and fishermen.

clue.text: Most of side bowled, as century seen here?

definitions.text: Most of side bowled, as century seen here?

indicators.note: means dropping the final letter of the word for side

parts.note: an edge is a side
B is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for bowled
taken as written
a ton is a century, a hundred runs in cricket

explanation.surface: A cricket report wonders whether a team was dismissed cheaply while a hundred was scored at this ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' trims EDGE to EDG. EDGBASTON is a Test cricket ground in Birmingham, England, so the whole clue describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being a famous cricket ground, it is a place where a batsman bowled or a century might be seen.

clue.text: Element of currency: I'm up for conversion

parts.note: the euro is the currency of much of Europe

indicators.note: conversion means changing form, so these letters are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone offers to change their money into euros.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for conversion' rearranges IMUP into PIUM. Conversion is a currency word, which hides its job.
explanation.definitionFit: Europium is a rare-earth chemical element, number 63 in the periodic table.

clue.text: Goes over and collects outside clubs

indicators.note: says the first word wraps around the second

parts.note: to collect a harvest is to reap it
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A caddie runs through the plan and gathers up the golf clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: To recap is to summarise or review, going back over what was said.

clue.text: Man's leaving Midlands town for country area

indicators.note: says those letters depart from the town's name

parts.note: Mansfield is a town in Nottinghamshire, in the English Midlands
the word taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A man moves out of a Midlands town to live in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: MANSFIELD is a town in Nottinghamshire, England; taking off MANS leaves the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A field is an enclosed stretch of open farmland in the countryside.

clue.text: Light shade from Scotland?

parts.note: a pale greyish-beige colour named after a staple Scottish food made from ground oats

explanation.surface: A paint chart names a pale colour after its Scottish origin.
explanation.walkthrough: The colour takes its name from ground oats, the Scottish porridge staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Oatmeal is a pale fawn colour, and ground oats are a classic Scottish foodstuff.

clue.text: It's best of all coming from France

definitions.text: It's best of all coming from France

parts.words: It's best of all coming from France
parts.note: a French phrase meaning the very finest, cream of the cream

explanation.surface: A boast that French produce beats everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: This borrowed French idiom means the elite, the very finest of a group.

clue.text: Cleo, a girl, becomes symbolic

indicators.note: says the letters turn into something else, a rearranged word

explanation.surface: Cleopatra, a mere girl, turns into a symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegoric writing carries a hidden symbolic meaning beneath its literal story.

clue.text: Organic compound obtained from a variety of trees

indicators.note: variety suggests a different form, so the letters are arranged differently

explanation.surface: A chemist extracts a substance from several kinds of tree.
explanation.definitionFit: An ester is an organic chemical formed from an acid and an alcohol.

clue.text: Watch, some say, for an Indian dish

indicators.note: says the word is to be heard, as some people pronounce it

parts.note: ticker is slang for a watch

explanation.surface: Someone hunts for a watch while ordering a curry.
explanation.walkthrough: TICKER is old slang for a watch (also for the heart).
explanation.definitionFit: Tikka is marinated meat cooked in a clay oven, a dish of Indian cuisine.

clue.text: Hope that goes up in smoke?

definitions.text: Hope that goes up in smoke?

parts.words: Hope that goes up in smoke?
parts.note: a hopeless fantasy, imagined as the vision of a smoker of opium

explanation.surface: An ambition that vanishes like burning paper.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase comes from opium smokers' visions, so the smoke is literal and figurative.
explanation.definitionFit: A fantastic, unrealistic plan or hope that will never come true.

clue.text: Infer the prisoner's honest

parts.note: a con is a convict, a prisoner; with the 's it gives CONS
true means honest or sincere

explanation.surface: Someone concludes that a jailbird is telling the truth.
explanation.definitionFit: To construe is to interpret or deduce a meaning from words or actions.

clue.text: Wrongly advised boss about piece of land

indicators.note: says the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: MD, managing director, is the boss of a firm
an isle is a piece of land in the sea

explanation.surface: A manager got bad guidance about some property.
explanation.definitionFit: To be misled is to have been given wrong guidance or led astray.

clue.text: Clever person, William, displacing No 3 in cricket, say

indicators.note: says one piece pushes out another and takes its place

parts.note: a cricket is an example of an insect
the third letter of the word for the insect
William Tell, the legendary Swiss archer

explanation.surface: A clever William replaces the number three batsman in a cricket team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cricket, say' looks like the sport; it is the chirping insect. TELL replaces its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Intellect can mean a person of great intelligence, a thinker.

clue.text: Med area right for producing rum

indicators.note: producing means making something new, so these letters are made into a new order

explanation.surface: A Mediterranean region is used for making rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for producing' rearranges MEDAREA with R. Demerara is also a sugar, but here it is the rum from Guyana.
explanation.definitionFit: Demerara is a dark rum made in Guyana, named after its river region.

clue.text: MIT leaves army equipment for student bodies

indicators.note: says those letters depart from the word

parts.note: munitions are military weapons and ammunition

explanation.surface: A university quits supplying the military to fund student clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: MIT, the American university, is taken out as written letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Student unions are organisations representing students at a university.

clue.text: Give free rein to take in alcohol

definitions.meaning: to let a desire or person have their way
to have a drink, to booze

explanation.surface: Advice to let oneself go and have a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To indulge is both to gratify a wish and, colloquially, to drink alcohol.

clue.text: Upright vicar returned old Thai coin

indicators.note: says the word is read backwards

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is the title of a vicar
a tical was a former silver coin of Siam

explanation.surface: A straight-laced vicar handed back an old coin from Thailand.
explanation.definitionFit: Vertical means standing straight up, perpendicular to the horizon.

clue.text: One account supporting the odd character of the heart

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece supporting another comes beneath it

parts.note: a card is an eccentric or amusing person
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone backs up an eccentric with a bank account.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardiac means relating to the heart, as in cardiac arrest.

clue.text: Food preserver incorporated in "Time" article

indicators.note: says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
Inc is the abbreviation for incorporated, used of companies

explanation.surface: A news magazine features a piece on food preservation.
explanation.definitionFit: A tin can is a metal container used for keeping food fresh.

clue.text: None cried when treatment applied for a particular gland

definitions.note: the adjective names a type of gland, the ductless kind

indicators.note: treatment means being processed, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: No one wept during medical treatment for a gland problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Endocrine glands secrete hormones straight into the blood rather than through ducts.

clue.text: Island company depending on artificial fur

indicators.note: in a down clue, hanging from above, so the first piece goes on top
artificial means not natural, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A business on an island relies on fake fur.
explanation.definitionFit: Corfu is a Greek island in the Ionian Sea.

clue.text: Class put back (including Year 1) for a number of lines

indicators.note: says the outer piece wraps around the inner
says the letters are read backwards

parts.note: CL is an abbreviation for class
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A school class is held back a year, with first-years included.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' gives LC; 'Year 1' looks like a school form but is two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyric is a short poem, or the words of a song, made up of lines.

clue.text: Fitter in the cable/rope business

indicators.note: says the answer sits inside the clue words that follow

explanation.surface: A mechanic works in the cable and rope trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Abler means more able, more fit for a task.

clue.text: Shooting off in the break?

parts.note: a pause in fighting, when guns stop firing

explanation.surface: Someone leaves quickly during the interval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shooting off' looks like dashing away; it means gunfire switched off during a truce.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceasefire is a temporary halt in fighting agreed between enemies.

clue.text: No new copy's involved in this case

definitions.text: No new copy's involved in this case

parts.words: No new copy's involved in this case
parts.note: describes the real thing, an original rather than a replica

explanation.surface: An investigator notes that no forgery is part of the matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something authentic and original, not a fake or imitation.
